lesson.text: Quick memory: who do you tell if something worries you? (A grown-up you trust.) Today: staying safe and kind online.
Before a new game or app, ask a grown-up. They help you choose good ones.
Your name, your school, where you live and photos of you stay private. Never share them online.
Someone you don't know sends a message? Don't answer: tell a grown-up.
Be kind online, just like in real life, and take breaks: stretch, have a drink, look out of the window.
Try it in the world: open Online City on the play tablet. Next: strangers, mean posts and passwords, on the Middle track.

exercises.prompt: You can tell someone online where you live.
Something online makes you sad. You...

exercises.hint: Which tells people where to find you?
Words can hurt, even on a screen.

exercises.prompt: A box pops up with a flashing button. You...
choices: close it and ask a grown-up
exercises.hint: Don't tap what you don't know.
Could it help someone find you?
exercises.explain: Where you live and photos of you stay private.

exercises.prompt: After playing for a long time, it's good to...
Telling a grown-up about a worrying message is the right thing to do.
Someone you don't know asks for a photo of you. You...
choices: don't send it and tell a grown-up
exercises.explain: Don't send it: tell a grown-up.

exercises.prompt: A message worries you: put it in order.
exercises.explain: Don't answer, then tell a grown-up.
